_source: Silk Road Trading Simulator Fandom Wiki, crawled 2026-09. Corrections below (2026-09-27) come from ~30 in-game purchase/sale breakdown screenshots (a tester's own trades), which itemize every modifier as its own line and let real gating rules be reverse-engineered from what does/doesn't fire.
_warning: Several values below are placeholders needing community confirmation — search this file for 'UNCONFIRMED' before treating any number as final.

supplyDemand._status: CORRECTED 2026-09-27: locally produced goods show NO supply/demand line in any screenshot (6 buys: Tyre candles, Damascus weapons, Palmyra yarn, Antioch silk, Samarkand ewer, Dunhuang Sancai all match base minus favorability lines exactly). Local production just means Distance Bonus = $0; there is no separate percentage discount. locallyProducedDiscount kept at 0 for reference only - calc.js no longer reads it. importedMarkup (20%) is only a fallback when the distance graph can't connect a pair.

Cosmopolitan City.description: +10% price bonus for traders from a different culture than the city's

Homogenous City.description: -10% price penalty for traders from a different culture than the city's

Capital City.description: +10% price increase for luxury goods ("Capital Luxury Trade" in-game)
Capital City.note: Re-gated to luxury goods (goods with originOnly, or category 'luxury'). Earlier gate was category craft or textile, but two Bosra (a Capital city) screenshots show NO Capital line on Earthenware or Books, both craft. All earlier confirmed hits (Byzantine Silk, Persian Carpets, Sancai Dragon Ware, Sogdian Ewer, Minakari Ware) are originOnly goods, and Sesame still gets none. Inferred from the Info Hub wording 'luxury goods' plus those screenshots.

Frontier City.description: +10% price bonus for tools and weapons
Frontier City.note: Corrected: was 'category:tools_weapons', which matched nothing (weapons/tools are category 'metal'). Gating on category metal would wrongly hit Iron Ingot, which screenshots show gets no Frontier line in Dunhuang/Jiayuguan. Confirmed by 'Frontier Tool Trade' +$13 on Weapons ($130) in Palmyra.

Desert City.description: +10% price bonus for food items (Info Hub; Fandom's Events page said 5%).

Earthquake Prone City.note: Same category bug as Frontier City (no 'tools' category exists) - changed to goods:tools. Not yet confirmed by a screenshot.

Ruined City.description: No goods traded here at all.

Fertile City.description: 10% price decrease for food items (Info Hub).
Fertile City.note: Sign is a guess: treated as a penalty-style trait like Homogenous. Unconfirmed by any itemized screenshot.

Oasis City.description: Recent conflict has limited the goods available for purchase here.
Oasis City.note: Info Hub. Used by Thantia and Mephaat, which are not in the calculator.

religionModifiers._source: SR:TS Information Hub 'Religions' page, captured via a headless-browser crawl that clicks through every carousel slide (a plain HTTP fetch only ever saw the first/active slide - confirmed via DevTools that the '>' button is a live JS-driven element, not a static list merely hidden by CSS).
religionModifiers._faithMechanic: Faith [points] are earned by praying at one's own religion's site, capped at 500 total / 100 per prayer session. Level 1 at 5 Faith, Level 2 at 120 Faith, Level 3 at 300 Faith. Each religion's effects below are gated behind reaching that level - they do NOT apply at Faith Level 0, unlike the previous (incorrect) version of this file which applied everything unconditionally the moment a religion was selected.
religionModifiers._buildingCities: Each religion's 'buildingCities' list traces to that religion's 'Location' field on the Religions page - i.e. which cities have that religion's building present. This is NOT the same as a city's own dominant religion in cities.json - e.g. Samarkand's dominant religion is Manichaeism, but it still appears in Christianity's buildingCities, meaning a Church exists there too (cosmopolitan cities host multiple faiths' buildings). Used for Christianity Level 1 (Church Hospitality) only - see christianBrothersGating note below for Level 2.
religionModifiers.christianBrothersGating: IMPORTANT: Christianity's Level 2 effect ('Brothers in Christ') is NOT gated on buildingCities, despite what its name suggests and despite earlier versions of this file assuming so. ~17 screenshot trades across 8 cities show it firing in every city EXCEPT the 4 Sasanian Empire cities (Ctesiphon, Susa, Ecbatana, Isfahan) - including firing in Samarkand, Dunhuang, and Jiayuguan, none of which are Christian-dominant or on the old buildingCities list's core set. The real gate, wired in calc.js's religionOwnModifiersDollar, is the city's empire not being in levels['2'].excludedEmpires (Sasanian Empire; Rashidun Caliphate was added after a Petra sale showed no Brothers in Christ line). Kept as a plain empire check rather than a data list since it matches the in-game text ('Brothers in Christ' implying solidarity against a specific rival empire, not literal church presence).

Christianity.buildingCitiesNote: Excludes Palmyra and Persepolis. Palmyra confirmed via screenshot: Church Hospitality did NOT fire there (places_of_worship: None on the wiki), despite Palmyra being Cosmopolitan/Capital-eligible under the old (wrong) gating - confirming Level 1 gates on building presence, not city traits.

1.name: Church Hospitality
1.gatingNote: Despite the name, this is gated on buildingCities (church presence), not the Capital/Cosmopolitan traits - confirmed by Palmyra (Cosmopolitan, no church) never firing it, while Ecbatana (Homogenous only, has a church) always does.

2.name: Brothers In Christ
2.gatingNote: See top-level christianBrothersGating note - gates on city.empire !== 'Sasanian Empire', not buildingCities.

1.status: UNCONFIRMED — applies to herbs and spices in a Monastery city, but 'herbs' isn't a good/category in goods.json yet. Per the user, herbs are upcoming game content not yet added - left unimplemented rather than guessed at.

2.status: Not applicable to this calculator — +300% Reputation from trading in a Monastery city is a reputation-GAIN mechanic. The calculator only tracks reputation RANK for gating/quest-money, it doesn't simulate reputation accumulation from trades.

Islam.note: Info Hub Religions page. Its description is still '?' there and its only location is Petra.

religionModifiers._jiayuguanNote: Jiayuguan added to Christianity/Zoroastrianism/Manichaeism/Mahayana Buddhism buildingCities per the infohub Religions page (Aug 2026 update); confirmed for Christianity by a Church Hospitality line firing there in screenshots.

Native.note: Same stat value as Fluent, but a distinct label/level in-game (Fluent = Level 3, Native = Level 4). Native is always tied to your culture and can't be independently selected.

reputationDiscount._status: WIRED. Rank 6 gives a 10% buy-only discount on goods: inside the empire for Byzantine/Sasanian, outside it for Sogdia/Tang (Info Hub). Confirmed by 5 Sasanian screenshots only; the outside variants and stacking across factions are unconfirmed. Rank 3's discount covers shops (cosmetics/animals), not goods, so it is not applied.

conflict.note: Weapons and all metal-category goods (Iron/Copper Ingot, Tools) share the 'metal' category in goods.json, matching the wiki's 'weapons and metal' wording.

distanceBonus.status: Cells present in Buy_Data_v2 are exact; the rest are extrapolated and UNCONFIRMED. Exotic rate is from one sale screenshot.

perks.name: Junk Hoarding
perks.status: Common only, per the Info Hub and a contributor. In game it is currently bugged and also boosts Rare and Exotic goods; that is modelled by bugRarities and only applies when 'Match game bugs' is on.
